item.title: Trump claims control of Strait of Hormuz as stalemate deepens
item.description: Stalemate between two countries deepens as President Trump mirrors Iran's demand for compensation and claims U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz

item.title: Trump secretly switched to different plane in Turkey amid Iran threat
item.description: Ahead of a flight from Turkey, President Trump secretly left Air Force One and was moved to another plane with the help of a catering truck, according to a source, as the U.S. grappled with a threat from Iran.

item.title: Powerball jackpot nears $1 billion after no one won $905 million grand prize
item.description: There were no winning tickets sold for Monday night's $905 million Powerball jackpot, so the estimated grand prize for Wednesday night's drawing will be at least $975 million, Powerball says.

item.title: 7.4 earthquake strikes western Colombia, killing at least 111 people
item.description: The 7.4 magnitude earthquake's epicenter was San José del Palmar, about 250 miles west of Colombia's capital, Bogota, officials said.

item.title: Doctors respond to Trump's vaccine executive order as kids head back to school
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday that lowers the recommended number of vaccines for children and encourages splitting up certain vaccines into separate doctor visits. Doctors spoke with CBS News about the order and suggested that parents speak with their children's pediatricians about what would be best for their kids.

item.title: In texts, Fauci discussed potential risks, benefits of COVID vaccine for pregnant women
item.description: Two Senate Republicans released a set of 2021 texts that show Dr. Anthony Fauci discussing how to "weigh the potential risks against the benefits" of pregnant women taking COVID-19 vaccines.

item.title: Trump signs order on vaccination recommendations
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on childhood vaccine schedules Monday.

item.title: 5 takeaways from Zuckerberg's essay on his vision for superintelligence
item.description: In a 6,500-word post, the Meta CEO argues that superintelligence should be shared "with as many people and businesses as possible."

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg's vision of superintelligent AI for everyone
item.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is making the case for putting superintelligent AI in the hands of everyone, not just a few companies or governments. Charles Rollet, tech correspondent for Business Insider, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Captain of boat that capsized in New York facing federal charges after mom, infant die
item.description: Manuel Hernandez, the boat's 46-year-old captain, was arrested on reckless endangerment charges and also charged in federal court with two counts of misconduct and neglect.

item.title: Man who allegedly arranged Tupac Shakur's 1996 killing is on trial in Las Vegas
item.description: The man who prosecutors say orchestrated the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, Duane "Keffe D" Davis, is on trial almost 30 years after the drive-by shooting in Las Vegas.

item.title: Previewing Tuesday's primaries in 5 states, including Wisconsin, Minnesota and South Carolina
item.description: Voters in five states are gearing up for another big primary day on Tuesday. Connecticut, Vermont, Minnesota and Wisconsin are holding elections for state and federal offices while South Carolina is having a special primary for late Sen. Lindsey Graham's open Senate seat. CBS News' Mark Strassmann, Jonah Kaplan and Taurean Small have more.

item.title: How have the goals of the Iran war evolved?
item.description: The Iranian regime is now saying it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. doesn't meet its demands, including compensation for the damage it has done in the more than five months since the start of the war. While the U.S. has reiterated that its top priority is ensuring that Iran can never achieve nuclear capabilities, having the strait fully open to traffic has become key. CBS News contributor Elliot Ackerman joins with analysis.

item.title: WNBA faces new controversy after Sky's DiJonai Carrington ejected over foul on Sophie Cunningham
item.description: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham, already at the center of a fight over transgender participation, took a flagrant foul from an opposing player who was ejected from the game. Jan Crawford has more details.

item.title: Chuck Grassley's beloved vacuum, Beth, has retired
item.description: Iowa Sen. Chuck Grassley has been posting little snapshots of his "old reliable" vacuum. But after nearly 50 years of service in the family, she has retired. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño items at Walmart, Target over salmonella risk
item.description: The recalled products with jalapeño were distributed at national retailers, including Walmart, Target and Trader Joe's, in 26 states.

item.title: Jackie, a beloved bald eagle from Big Bear, dies after attack by 2 other eagles
item.description: Jackie, of the beloved bald eagle duo Jackie and Shadow, watched by millions on the Big Bear live feed, has died.

item.title: Jury selection begins in Tupac Shakur murder trial
item.description: Nearly 30 years after the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, jury selection is underway for the man charged in connection with the murder, Duane "Keffe D" Davis. Celebrity attorney Chris Melcher joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño products potentially contaminated with salmonella
item.description: Taylor Farms, the company linked to this summer's lettuce-related parasite outbreak, is now recalling jalapeño pepper products after new concerns about salmonella. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Wildfires ravage the West: Details and the forecast
item.description: Hot and dry conditions out west fueled at least 200 major wildfires across the U.S. and Canada. Jonathan Vigliotti reports from Spokane, Washington, and Paul Deanno has the forecast.

item.title: Trump orders new vaccine recommendations, experts urge parents to listen to their kids' doctors
item.description: As kids head back to school amid the worst measles outbreak in decades, President Trump signed an executive order slashing the number of vaccines recommended for children. Ed O'Keefe has the details and Dr. Jon LaPook discusses what parents should know.

item.title: Trump demands Iran pay compensation following new conditions for reopening strait
item.description: President Trump signaled he would be piling economic pressure on Iran as the stalemate continued and Tehran laid out new conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: 8/10: CBS Evening News
item.description: Trump called for fewer vaccines in a new executive order; a catastrophic earthquake hit Colombia.

item.title: 8/10: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump signs executive order updating childhood vaccine recommendations; primary day for five states on Tuesday.

item.title: Court clears way for social media addiction suits against tech giants
item.description: Appeals court ruling could open the door to a flood of litigation against Google, Meta and other social media players.

item.title: Why Taylor Farms faces scrutiny over salmonella and cyclospora outbreaks
item.description: Despite a rash of foodborne illnesses in recent months, one expert said the nation's food supply is "remarkably safe." Here's what to know.

item.title: Contiguous U.S. breaks its record for hottest month ever, NOAA says
item.description: Temperatures last month averaged 76.9 degrees Fahrenheit as above-average warmth blanketed the U.S.

item.title: Big Bear bald eagle Jackie has died, California veterinary center says
item.description: "It is with profound sadness that we share that [Jackie] passed away in the early hours of this morning, following more than three weeks of intensive medical care," Ojai Raptor Center said.

item.title: Blanche sworn in as attorney general, formally taking reins at DOJ
item.description: Todd Blanche was sworn in as attorney general after the Senate narrowly voted to confirm the president's former defense lawyer to helm the Justice Department over the weekend.

item.title: AOC shares her egg-freezing journey. Here's what to know about the process.
item.description: "This is a choice that I am making to feel more in control of my life," said 36-year-old Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
